Hi there, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Dr. Lee, and I’m the perinatal mental-health specialist on the team. I’m going to walk you through a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived—especially over the past seven days—so we can be sure you’re getting the support you deserve. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me otherwise, and there are no right or wrong answers.

We’ll go through 10 questions together. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer in your own words. If anything feels too hard to talk about, just let me know and we can pause.

Ready to start? Here’s the first question:

Over the past week, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you smile, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

Um… I still smile sometimes, like when the baby squeezes my finger or when my toddler brings me a picture she colored. But a lot of the little things—my favorite show, texting friends, even the smell of my coffee in the morning—feel kind of flat, like I’m just going through the motions. I wouldn’t say it’s totally gone, but it’s definitely dulled.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I do laugh every now and then—like yesterday when my husband made that silly face with the pacifier stuck on his chin—but it feels kind of forced or short-lived. Most of the time I’m too tired or preoccupied to really find things funny the way I used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I mean, I still plan things—like a coffee outing with my mom-friends or getting a pumpkin-spice latte—but when the time comes, I’m mostly just tired or worried the baby will fuss. It feels more like something I “should” enjoy than something I actually look forward to.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like last night the baby wouldn’t settle for two hours, and I kept thinking maybe I ate something that upset his tummy, or I’m not doing the routine right. Rationally I know babies just cry, but the thought still pops in that I must be missing something or doing it wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Mostly it’s about the baby. I’ll lie down and suddenly wonder if his breathing sounded weird, or I’ll replay the way he spit-up earlier and worry it’s something serious. There isn’t always a clear trigger—it just feels like my mind hops from one “what-if” to the next, even when everything looks fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A couple of times. Like yesterday, right before I was about to pump, my heart started racing and I felt this wave of dread, like something bad was about to happen—even though nothing was going on. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me shaky and kind of on edge the rest of the evening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah… some days it feels like the second I finish one thing—dishes, diaper, laundry—there’s already another pile waiting. I’ll be rocking the baby and think, “I can’t remember if I ate lunch,” and suddenly I’m on the edge of tears just from the constant cycle. I’m keeping up, but it feels like I’m barely a step ahead, and by evening I’m completely wiped.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s not every night—maybe three or four nights this week. I’ll finally get the baby down, crawl into bed myself, and then my brain just keeps spinning with to-do lists or worries that the baby will wake up any second. I end up lying there for an hour or two, drifting in and out, and when I do fall asleep it feels light, like I’m still half-listening for cries.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way some of the time—maybe every other day. It’s not constant, but it hits out of nowhere, like a heavy blanket that just settles on me. I’ll be folding tiny onesies and suddenly feel like crying, though I couldn’t always tell you why.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not a lot—maybe twice this week. Once when I spilled the freshly-pumped milk on the floor and once when my mom left after dropping off groceries. Both times the tears came fast, then stopped almost as quickly. It’s not an everyday thing.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed and exhausted, sure, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 19: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – Brief Summary  

<sym>Presenting symptoms</sym>  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, sense of “heaviness” (Q8)  
- Marked reduction in pleasure/anticipation (Q1, Q2)  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt over routine infant care (Q3)  
- Unwarranted anxiety, racing thoughts, situational panic sensations (Q4, Q5)  
- Subjective overwhelm, feeling “barely a step ahead” (Q6)  
- Initial insomnia secondary to intrusive worries (Q7)  
- Infrequent crying spells linked to minor stressors (Q9)  

<med>Screening significance</med>  
- Meets clinical threshold indicators for probable minor–moderate postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety features  
- No current self-harm ideation reported (Q10) – low acute safety risk  

Risk factors / pattern  
- Symptoms present ≥ several days per week, interfering with sleep and functional coping  
- Typical postpartum stressors (fatigue, infant care demands) exacerbating, rather than causing, mood disturbance  

Next steps (screening only)  
- Continue monitoring with validated instrument (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS)  
- Consider referral for comprehensive evaluation if symptoms persist or worsen
